**Phases of the Respiratory cycle** 

 ![](/content/exams/anzca/2020/B/6/standard-image44.png){fig-alt="Normal capnogram with respiratory phases, end-tidal point and alpha and beta angles"}

1.  Inspiratory baseline - reflects inspiratory gasses 
2.  Expiratory upstroke, transition from dead space gas to alveolar gas
3.  Alveolar plateau represents alveolar gas
4.  End tidal point of EtCO2 measurement 

> Phase 0 - inspiratory downstroke 

**Information obtained from capnograph**

**Patient information:**

1.  Confirmation of endotracheal placement and/or effective ventilation with multiple normal waveforms
    - Right main bronchus intubation may show bifid capnograph 
2.  Adequacy of ventilation and perfusion, rising or abnormally low EtCO2 may represent under ventilation or low perfusion states 
3.  Expiratory resistance / obstruction with slow ‘shark fin’ rise in CO2 at expiration 

**Equipment Information **

1.  Soda lime exhaustion →↑inspiratory baseline CO2
2.  Circuit disconnection 
3.  inspiratory / expiratory valve malfunction
